claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires preparation temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically contains residual porosity.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 typically contains microcracks.
Residual porosity and microcracks compromise the strength and structural integrity of ZrB2.
Residual defects make conventional ZrB2 susceptible to degradation during liquid-plating exposure.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 5 wt% SiC to the ZrB2 precursor powder before sintering.
Adding a few weight percent SiC enables ZrB2 densification at approximately 2000–2200 °C rather than above 2300 °C.
SiC acts as a reactive sintering aid in ZrB2.
SiC forms a transient liquid phase during ZrB2 sintering at the proposed temperatures.
The SiC-induced transient liquid phase enhances grain-boundary diffusion and mass transport.
Enhanced diffusion and mass transport produce a denser microstructure with fewer pores and microcracks.
Residual defects and porosity serve as nucleation sites for holes during exposure to a corrosive liquid-plating bath.
Reducing residual defects and porosity will reduce plating-induced hole formation.
SiC-doped ZrB2 prepared at lower temperature will have mechanical integrity comparable to or better than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SiC-doped ZrB2 will have significantly lower porosity than conventionally prepared ZrB2.
SiC-doped ZrB2 will exhibit fewer holes and component failures during long-duration liquid-plating exposure.
The proposed intervention is expected to be effective between approximately 2000 and 2200 °C.
Efficacy outside the stated preparation-temperature and liquid-plating service boundaries is unverified.

contradictions.description: The experimental design sinters both doped and undoped sets at 2000 °C and 2200 °C, but the stated baseline and falsification rule require comparison against conventional undoped ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C. No above-2300 °C control is included in the described design.
